strings.title: Give and Take
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: When one number is close to a hundred or a thousand, give it what it needs from the other number. The total stays the same: 298 + 145 = 300 + 143.
strings.keywords: give and take, friendly number, close to, total stays the same, compensate
watchFor: Making the friendly number but forgetting to take from the other (298 + 145 = 445): ask "Where did the 2 come from?"
Taking from the wrong number, or giving too much: ask "How much does 298 need to make 300?"
Lining up the algorithm when the numbers are friendly: ask "Is one number close to a hundred?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why does the total stay the same?" Land: moving an amount from one number to the other doesn't change the total. Make one number friendly, then the adding is easy.

problems.notes: Look for: a quick friendly sum. Ask: "Hold on to this one." Model: split 300 + 145
Look for: 298 gets 2 from 145: 300 + 143. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Word choice: "give and take". Model: givetake 298 + 145 = 300 + 143

responses.tip: Gave 2 but didn't take it. Ask: where did the 2 come from?

problems.notes: Look for: 500 + 237. Ask: "What does 499 need?" Model: givetake 499 + 238 = 500 + 237
Look for: 2000 + 345. Ask: "Is it the same idea with thousands?" Model: givetake 1998 + 347 = 2000 + 345
Look for: 4000 + 2001. Ask: "Which number should give?" Model: givetake 3995 + 2006 = 4000 + 2001

responses.tip: Either number can give. Ask: which was easier?
Added the 5 back instead of taking it away. Ask: is 3995 more or less than 4000?

problems.notes: Look for: 1500 + 2500. Ask: "What do you notice about these numbers?" Model: givetake 1499 + 2501 = 1500 + 2500

responses.tip: A neat one: both become friendly.
